title: Synthetic workload probe — microsegment pricing/latency elasticity study
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Run a controlled synthetic workload experiment across representative microsegments (SMB chatbots, enterprise search, edge-RAG) to quantify how customers trade latency vs price when switching model variants or deployment modes. Objective is to produce a decision matrix that links percent price change, tail latency, and user-visible metric degradation to predicted churn and inferred willingness-to-pay for latency improvements. This will inform pricing/packaging and Dedicated vs Hosted recommendations for near-term GTM motions.
hypotheses: SMB customers are more price-sensitive than latency-sensitive for batch embedding workloads
Enterprise search customers show high willingness-to-pay for 50ms median latency improvements under SLAs
Edge-RAG microsegments prefer local/private deployments even at higher cost when latency variability exceeds 200ms
methodology: 1) Define 3 microsegments and their synthetic workload profiles (QPS, sequence length distribution, typical prompt templates). 2) Create parametric workload generator that can vary per-token price proxy (model variant/quantization) and inject controlled latency distributions. 3) Run paired A/B probes across hosted, dedicated, and private stacks to measure quality (BLEU/ROUGE/embedding cosine drift where applicable), 99th and median latency, and cost-per-successful-request. 4) Fit elasticity curves and compute tipping points where customers are expected to switch deployment or model family.
acceptance_criteria:
- Experiment artifacts (workload generator, configs) checked into GH and linked.
- Raw telemetry stored in market-lab project dataset.
- Elasticity curves for at least 3 microsegments plotted and explained.
- Decision matrix with clear thresholds (price delta, latency delta) and recommended packaging actions.
- Stakeholder review completed (PM/Eng/Revenue Ops) and runbook for follow-up experiments created.

Implement workload generator and parametric knobs (owner: Eng)
Instrument telemetry capture and tagging (owner: Eng)

Quality evaluation and drift measurement (owner: Research)

Create follow-up experiment backlog based on results (owner: PM)
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: Synthetic workloads may not capture edge-case prompt distributions. Mitigation: seed runs with real telemetry-derived prompts from anonymized customers and include a small 'field' sample for validation.

Risk: Cost attribution differences between Hosted and Dedicated make apples-to-apples comparison hard. Mitigation: normalize to per-successful-request using identical quality thresholds and include sensitivity analysis for kernel-level inefficiencies.
Risk: Time spent on instrumentation delays GTM decisions. Mitigation: run a minimum viable probe on a single microsegment first (SMB embeddings) and iterate.
